status: Engineering source review; not a new extraction, independent scientific validation, or canonical atlas admission
purpose: Test whether broad Material State components hide distinctions needed to compare spatial, multiomic and temporal assays.
scope: Six primary papers. Selected fulltext Methods and workflow explanations were read for CITE-seq, DBiT-seq, SHARE-seq and SLAM-seq. Original Spatial Transcriptomics and Slide-seq were inspected at main-text workflow/figure-caption level; their original supplementary Methods were not successfully retrieved. No full-paper comprehensive review is claimed.
revisit_reason: The user challenged whether components and the five proposed Material State fields are scientifically useful. These examples specifically test molecular origin, reporter identity, prepared context, spatial addressing and branch routing; they are not unchanged extraction reruns.

read_sections: Figures 1 and 2 captions on printed pages 79-80
cases.read_limit: Primary paper mirrored in a university course; original supplementary Methods not obtained. Text inspection only; no numerical measurements inferred from OCR.
cases.prepared_material: Tissue section over an array of positional capture primers; captured mRNA is copied into cDNA associated with array-feature identifiers.
cases.essential_distinction: The probe includes a capture region, spatial barcode, UMI, cleavage site and amplification/sequencing functions. DNA alone does not identify whether the molecule is a capture primer or RNA-derived reporter.
cases.measurement_link: Transcript-derived sequences are assigned to capture features using positional barcodes and image registration; a feature is not automatically an individual cell.
cases.graph_use: Locate the operation that converts physical array position into a recoverable sequence identifier. Keep the coordinate map as a required information dependency.

read_sections: Spatial cell-type assignment and stereological caveat preceding Figure 2
cases.read_limit: Supplementary docx returned a browser challenge and publisher PDF access failed; no supplement-level recipe claim.
cases.prepared_material: A monolayer of DNA-barcoded beads whose barcode positions have been decoded; a frozen tissue section supplies RNA captured by those beads.
cases.essential_distinction: The beads are randomly arranged and their sequence-to-position map is measured. A bead preparation without that map is chemically similar but cannot provide the same spatial attribution.
cases.measurement_link: Sequenced transcript tags are mapped to bead positions. One bead can sample material from more than one cell type.
cases.graph_use: Distinguish spatial capture on decoded bead arrays from capture on predefined spatial arrays, while retaining their shared RNA capture purpose.

read_sections: STAR Methods: tissue handling and fixation
cases.prepared_material: Fixed tissue containing RNA-derived cDNA, subsequently carrying two spatial barcode identities introduced through orthogonal microfluidic channels.
cases.essential_distinction: Barcoding occurs in tissue before lysis, rather than requiring RNA transfer to a barcoded capture surface. Later cDNA recovery uses streptavidin beads; bead use therefore has a different role from Slide-seq spatial capture.
cases.measurement_link: Combined barcodes identify channel-intersection pixels. The paper explicitly states these do not directly resolve single cells. The optional antibody-tag branch reports a selected protein panel.
cases.graph_use: Compare where identity is attached and what material is retained at that point; do not match all bead-associated cDNA as the same spatial encoding operation.

read_sections: ONLINE METHODS: Conjugation of Antibodies to DNA-barcoding oligonucleotides
cases.prepared_material: Cells stained with DNA-tagged antibodies; after droplet lysis, endogenous mRNAs and synthetic poly(A)-tailed antibody oligonucleotides are captured on oligo(dT) beads.
cases.essential_distinction: The antibody tag is synthetic DNA reporting antibody identity, not endogenous RNA or protein sequence. The Methods explicitly invoke reverse transcriptase's DNA-dependent polymerase activity to copy the tag. Antibody-derived products and transcript-derived cDNA are separated by size for library preparation.
cases.measurement_link: Cell identifiers associate antibody-tag counts and transcript counts with the same partition. This is a joint measurement, not direct sequencing of protein molecules.
cases.graph_use: Find adoption of an RNA-library capture interface by a synthetic protein reporter; retain reporter origin and primer/handle requirements even when both final branches are DNA.

cases.prepared_material: Fixed cells or nuclei retain transposed genomic DNA and biotin-tagged RNA-derived cDNA while split-pool barcodes are applied. Reverse crosslinking then releases the barcoded molecules.
cases.essential_distinction: Both molecular products are DNA, but their origin and handles differ. Streptavidin capture recovers the biotin-tagged cDNA on beads, while the supernatant containing transposed genomic fragments proceeds to the ATAC library branch.
cases.measurement_link: Shared barcode combinations link chromatin accessibility and RNA expression at the cell level; they do not establish a same-molecule association.
cases.graph_use: A query must distinguish RNA-derived DNA from genomic fragments and recover their separate routes. DNA-only classification erases the assay's branch separation and co-measurement design.

cases.prepared_material: Total RNA from metabolically labeled cells, containing labeled and unlabeled transcripts, followed by chemical derivatization of incorporated 4-thiouridine.
cases.essential_distinction: Iodoacetamide modifies the incorporated thiolated nucleotide. The distinguishing signal is generated during copying and appears as excess T-to-C changes in sequencing data; neither RNA nor modified RNA alone specifies this mechanism.
cases.measurement_link: The chemical mark supports synthesis-window or turnover inference under the labeling design. It is not an exact molecule birth timestamp and does not require physical isolation of all newly synthesized RNA.
cases.graph_use: Separate the metabolic mark, its chemical derivatization and its sequence readout; compare alternatives that enrich marked molecules versus convert the mark into sequence evidence.

design_inferences_not_paper_claims: Lead a State description with the source-described preparation, not a bag of broad substance types. Cells, a tissue section, an RNA eluate and a cDNA library are preparation identities at different workflow boundaries.
Retain material origin separately from chemistry: genomic DNA, RNA-derived cDNA and synthetic antibody tags may all be DNA but carry different evidence and follow different routes.
Use constituent-level detail only when it locates a transformation, a consequential physical relationship or an information carrier. Do not enumerate every constituent of a cell or reaction mixture.
Put substrate, catalyst and reagent roles on their participation in an Operation. A bead or oligonucleotide does not have one universal role across the atlas.

Keep assay target-to-reporter interpretation at the assay level, but anchor each reporter and encoding transition to concrete State/Operation records. Otherwise agents cannot identify where information was recorded or lost.

A physical State alone is not enough for spatial attribution: barcode-to-coordinate maps and their registration provenance are data dependencies. Do not imply the physical barcode alone determines a position.

A source preparation name is not sufficient normalization. Conditional descriptors must expose origin, selected population, end chemistry/functional sequence regions, support/compartment and identity/routing when they distinguish the compared operations.

The minimum useful comparison unit is a transformation with prepared input, prepared output and local roles. Same RNA/DNA labels, same bead use or same enzyme name do not prove equivalence or historical influence.

critique_of_parent_minimal_rule.supported: A source-described preparation plus conditional consequential descriptors is more useful and compact than requiring a universal exhaustive components inventory. Operation-local roles and assay-level target/reporter separation resolve concrete ambiguities in these cases.
must_add_or_clarify: Source labels require normalization with preserved literal source wording; source authors can call synthetic DNA products cDNA or refer to targets when describing reporters. Naming must not override the actual stated molecular origin.
Preparation descriptions must preserve both molecular origin and current chemical form; source identity cannot be reduced to DNA/RNA type.
Attribution is partly physical and partly a data dependency, especially the measured barcode-to-coordinate map in Slide-seq.
Independent branches and co-measurement units must remain explicit: same cell or pixel does not imply same molecule or direct molecular interaction.

Conditional requirements must be comparison- and evidence-sensitive. They should request a missing differentiator rather than invent it or force a source-level block into a complete molecular reaction.

candidate_competency_checks: Retrieve the two SHARE-seq products that are both DNA and explain why one is bead-bound while the other is in the supernatant.
Identify which CITE-seq read sequence reports an endogenous transcript and which reports a synthetic antibody tag; do not label both as biological RNA measurements.
Distinguish the role of beads in Slide-seq spatial capture from their later purification role in DBiT-seq.
Find the required mapping data that converts a Slide-seq bead barcode into spatial position.
Identify where SLAM-seq's temporal chemical mark becomes sequence evidence and which stage still contains a mixed labeled/unlabeled RNA population.
Reject same-cell claims inferred only from a DBiT spatial pixel or same-molecule claims inferred only from paired SHARE-seq cell barcodes.
